correctness.rationale: After neighborhood observation the unseen cells are exactly the empty-row by empty-column rectangle. With both dimensions at least two, every observed vertex has zero or at least two unseen neighbors; with one dimension one and the other positive, each unseen cell has a forcing witness along its column or row, respectively, in the same simultaneous round. With a dimension zero no force is needed. Exact support counting via inclusion–exclusion forbids i specified rows and j columns and leaves (a−i)(b−j) free cells. This also removes the empty selection, with H(0,0)=1. Minimality under the disjunction of the two thresholds requires each cell to be indispensable for every satisfied threshold. This produces the three claimed types, and the joint type forces a square and a partial permutation. On m<n, m−1 rows chosen with singleton occupancies give m n^(m−1) sets and the column family is counted by surjections onto at most m−2 rows; the second type is nonempty precisely when m≥3. On a square, the two singleton families overlap in m²(m−1)! partial permutations. Thus the two extremal formulas include the thin-board boundary and the long-set example. Fresh exhaustive direct adjacency/forcing replays checked 135,696 subsets on six boards, including 2×6 and transposed 5×3, checking both polynomials, minimality and the parallel-round statement; for 3×5 the minimum-family count is 75 and the size-four count is 15. Finite enumeration is corroboration, not the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The scalar minimum is known and receives no originality credit. The supported contribution is the structural all-set and inclusion-minimal classification, including closed counts and the minimal-set spectrum, not the general polynomial definition or inclusion–exclusion technique. Later catalogue findings explicitly duplicate the support criterion and all-set polynomial, but their inspected findings do not give the inclusion-minimal spectrum. Accessible primary evidence on older diameter-two and product results does not establish coverage of the spectrum; the plausible inaccessible statements are named as residual risks, not treated as negative evidence.
residual_risks: The 2014 diameter-two, 2008 product and especially 2016 Cartesian-product primary texts could contain stronger statements than the evidence available; they remain uninspected after lawful retrieval attempts.
Later overlapping catalogue dates do not resolve discovery priority; the comparison is statement-level, not a priority determination.

value.rationale: A closed histogram of all successful and all deletion-minimal placements on a standard graph family extends the previously known minimum. In particular the minimal spectrum distinguishes small optimum placements from long irreducible ones, with an unbounded ratio on 3×n boards. The support criterion and counts permit direct evaluation and isolate a meaningful distinction from ordinary or connected domination.
